packs.blurb: Every sovereign state — 195 of them — with flags, capitals and where they sit.

packs.name: African countries
packs.blurb: All 54, from the Maghreb to the Cape — the set most people can name fewest of.

packs.name: European countries
packs.blurb: Including the microstates and every post-Yugoslav border.

packs.name: Asian countries
packs.blurb: Central, East, South and Southeast Asia, plus the Gulf.

packs.name: South American countries
packs.blurb: Twelve sovereign states and one French department.

packs.name: Central America & Mexico
packs.blurb: The isthmus, north to south.

packs.name: The Middle East

packs.name: Territories & dependencies

packs.name: The Caribbean

packs.name: Canadian provinces & territories
packs.blurb: Thirteen units, ten capitals you should know cold and three you probably do not.

packs.name: US states

packs.name: Indian states

packs.name: Japanese prefectures
packs.blurb: Forty-seven prefectures, Hokkaido to Okinawa.

packs.name: Australian states
packs.blurb: Six states and two mainland territories.

packs.name: German states
packs.blurb: The sixteen Bundesländer.

packs.name: Russian federal subjects

packs.name: Argentine provinces
packs.blurb: Twenty-three provinces and Buenos Aires.

packs.name: Nigerian states
packs.blurb: Thirty-six states and the Federal Capital Territory.

packs.name: South African provinces

packs.name: Indonesian provinces
packs.blurb: Across the whole archipelago.

packs.name: Swiss cantons

packs.name: Dutch provinces

packs.name: Egyptian governorates

packs.name: Kenyan provinces
packs.blurb: The former eight provinces, as Natural Earth draws them.

packs.name: Pakistani provinces
packs.blurb: Provinces and territories.

packs.name: Vietnamese provinces
packs.blurb: North to south.

packs.name: Philippine provinces
packs.blurb: Across the archipelago.

packs.name: Colombian departments
packs.blurb: Thirty-two departments.

packs.name: Chilean regions
packs.blurb: North to south down the longest country.

packs.name: Peruvian regions
packs.blurb: Coast, sierra and selva.

packs.name: Polish voivodeships
packs.blurb: Sixteen voivodeships.

packs.name: Turkish provinces
packs.blurb: Eighty-one provinces.

packs.name: South Korean provinces

packs.name: Spanish autonomous communities

packs.name: French regions

packs.name: The United Kingdom

packs.blurb: Where the largest cities on Earth actually are — most of them not where people guess.

packs.name: Canadian cities
packs.blurb: Every city worth the name, and which province it is in.

packs.name: US cities

packs.name: European cities

packs.name: African cities

packs.name: Asian cities

groups.name: The Greater Antilles
groups.blurb: The four large islands of the northern Caribbean — around 90% of the land area of the whole West Indies.
groups.note: Hispaniola is one island holding two countries, Haiti and the Dominican Republic. The Cayman Islands are sometimes counted in and sometimes not.

groups.name: The Lesser Antilles
groups.blurb: The long arc from the Virgin Islands south to Trinidad, plus the islands along the Venezuelan coast.

groups.name: The Leeward Islands
groups.blurb: The northern half of the Lesser Antilles arc, from the Virgin Islands down to Guadeloupe.
groups.note: The name is from sailing: the Leewards lie downwind of the Windwards on the prevailing north-easterly trade wind. Dominica is the sore point — the old British colony of the Leeward Islands ran down to include it, but modern geographic usage puts it in the Windwards.

groups.name: The Windward Islands
groups.blurb: The southern half of the arc, taking the trade wind first.
groups.note: Barbados is grouped with the Windwards in colonial and cricketing usage but lies about 150 km east of the arc, on its own shelf.

groups.name: The Grenadines
groups.blurb: The chain of small islands strung between Saint Vincent and Grenada, split between the two countries.
groups.note: Carriacou and Petite Martinique belong to Grenada; everything north of them to Saint Vincent. Petite Martinique, Palm Island, Petit Saint Vincent and the Tobago Cays are all real and all absent here — Natural Earth does not draw them at any resolution.

groups.name: The Lucayan Archipelago
groups.blurb: The Bahamas and the Turks and Caicos — the same limestone bank, two jurisdictions, and not in the Caribbean Sea at all.
groups.note: They sit in the Atlantic north of Cuba. Calling them Caribbean is cultural rather than oceanographic.

groups.name: The ABC Islands
groups.blurb: Aruba, Bonaire and Curaçao, off the Venezuelan coast — Dutch, dry, and outside the hurricane belt.

groups.name: The SSS Islands
groups.blurb: Saba, Sint Eustatius and Sint Maarten — the Dutch islands 900 km north of the ABCs.

groups.name: The Virgin Islands
groups.blurb: One archipelago under three flags: British, American, and the Spanish Virgins that belong to Puerto Rico.

groups.name: The Leeward Antilles
groups.blurb: The chain along the South American shelf — continental islands, not part of the volcanic arc.

groups.name: The Nordic countries
groups.blurb: Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland and Iceland, with the Faroes, Greenland and Åland.
groups.note: Not the same as Scandinavia: Finland is Nordic but not Scandinavian, and Iceland only arguably so.

groups.name: Scandinavia
groups.blurb: Strictly the peninsula and Denmark — Norway, Sweden and Denmark.

groups.name: The Baltic states
groups.blurb: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.

groups.name: The Low Countries
groups.blurb: Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

groups.name: Iberia
groups.blurb: The peninsula: Spain, Portugal, Andorra and Gibraltar.

groups.name: The Balkans
groups.blurb: The peninsula between the Adriatic and the Black Sea.
groups.note: Slovenia, Romania and the European sliver of Türkiye are in or out depending on whether the definition is physical, historical or political.

groups.name: The British Isles
groups.blurb: The archipelago: Great Britain, Ireland and the surrounding islands.
groups.note: The term is disputed in Ireland; "Britain and Ireland" or "these islands" is the usual alternative.

groups.name: The Visegrád Group
groups.blurb: Poland, Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary.

groups.name: The Caucasus
groups.blurb: Georgia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, between the Black Sea and the Caspian.

groups.name: The Maghreb
groups.blurb: North-west Africa: Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and Mauritania.

groups.name: The Sahel
groups.blurb: The belt between the Sahara and the savanna, west to east.

groups.name: The Horn of Africa
groups.blurb: Somalia, Ethiopia, Eritrea and Djibouti.

groups.name: The African Great Lakes
groups.blurb: The states around Victoria, Tanganyika and the western rift.

groups.name: Southern Africa
groups.blurb: The states south of the Congo and Zambezi basins.

groups.name: Central Asia
groups.blurb: The five former Soviet republics between the Caspian and China.

groups.name: The Levant
groups.blurb: The eastern Mediterranean seaboard.

groups.name: The Gulf states
groups.blurb: The six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council.

groups.name: Mainland Southeast Asia
groups.blurb: The peninsula: Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam and peninsular Malaysia.

groups.name: Melanesia
groups.blurb: The "black islands" of the south-west Pacific.

groups.name: Polynesia
groups.blurb: The great triangle — Hawaii, New Zealand and Easter Island at its corners.

groups.name: Micronesia
groups.blurb: The "small islands" north of the equator in the western Pacific.

groups.name: The Greater Sunda Islands
groups.blurb: Borneo, Sumatra, Java and Sulawesi.
groups.note: Borneo alone is divided between three countries — Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.

groups.name: Central America
groups.blurb: The seven states of the isthmus.

groups.name: The Southern Cone
groups.blurb: Argentina, Chile and Uruguay, with Paraguay and southern Brazil sometimes added.

groups.name: The Andean states
groups.blurb: The countries the cordillera runs through.

groups.name: The Guianas
groups.blurb: Guyana, Suriname and French Guiana — the only part of South America that is not Spanish- or Portuguese-speaking.

groups.name: The Maritimes
groups.blurb: Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Prince Edward Island.
groups.note: Add Newfoundland and Labrador and it becomes Atlantic Canada — the distinction is the common trap.

groups.name: Atlantic Canada
groups.blurb: The Maritimes plus Newfoundland and Labrador.

groups.name: The Prairie provinces
groups.blurb: Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta.

groups.name: The territorial North
groups.blurb: Yukon, the Northwest Territories and Nunavut — 40% of Canada’s area, 0.3% of its people.

groups.name: New England
groups.blurb: Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, Massachusetts, Rhode Island and Connecticut.

groups.name: The Four Corners
groups.blurb: The only point in the United States where four states meet.

groups.name: The Pacific Northwest
groups.blurb: Washington, Oregon and Idaho — and British Columbia, if you are drawing Cascadia.

groups.name: The Great Lakes states
groups.blurb: The eight states touching the lakes.

A single volcano, 13 km², with the shortest commercial runway in the world.

The flat limestone eastern wing, separated from Basse-Terre by the Rivière Salée.

The third island of Antigua and Barbuda: an uninhabited rock with a literary "kingdom" attached to it.
The largest of the Grenadines, and one of the last places with an aboriginal whaling quota.

The largest of the Bay Islands — English-speaking, and Honduran only since 1861.
